AZ.note: Lowest interest bid, capped at 16%/yr simple (42-18053); redeemable within 3 years and until treasurer deed delivered (42-18152).

CO.sourceTitle: Denver Treasury - Tax Lien Sale; Larimer County Treasurer - Tax Lien Sale (C.R.S. 39-12-103)
CO.note: Formula (Sept 1 federal discount rate + 9, rounded) confirmed; 2026 sale rate is 13%. Highest bidder/premium (premium not refunded); deed application after 3 years unredeemed (Denver).

changes.note: Denver and Larimer County treasurers list 13% for the 2026 sale (Sept 1, 2026 discount rate 3.75% + 9, rounded). The 8% floor was not re-read.

CT.note: §12-157: public auction to highest bidder; redemption with 18%/yr interest within six months of sale (60 days if abandoned). Note: §12-157 sells the property itself (deed held unrecorded during redemption); CT municipalities may also assign liens (§12-195h).

changes.note: §12-157(f): redemption not later than six months after sale, or 60 days for abandoned property.

DC.note: Read §47-1360 (redeem any time until foreclosure is final) and §47-1361, but the interest rate and foreclosure-filing timing were not found in the text read; not confirmed.

DE.sourceTitle: 9 Del. C. ch. 87 subch. IV (Kent and Sussex) (delcode.delaware.gov)
DE.note: Kent/Sussex: 1-year redemption with 20% interest (§8776). New Castle 60-day/15% provisions and sheriff role not re-read this run.

FL.note: 197.172: certificate max 18%/yr; 197.432: lowest interest rate bid in 1/4% steps; 197.502: deed application 2 years after April 1 of issuance year.

GA.sourceTitle: DeKalb County Tax Commissioner - Tax Sales
GA.note: Redeem within 12 months; 20% first year then 10% each added year; sold to highest bidder. County source, not statute text.

IA.note: 447.1: 2% per month redemption interest confirmed. 447.9: expiration notice may be served after 1 year 9 months from sale - confirmed. 446.16: winner is bidder accepting the smallest percentage of the parcel, not a dollar premium.

changes.note: Iowa Code §446.16(1): purchaser is the person who pays the total due for the smallest percentage of the parcel; minimum 1%.

ID.note: Redemption rights expire 14 months from issuance of the tax deed to the county (earlier if county sells/transfers). Sale method not re-read.

IL.note: Penalty bid max 9%, multiplied per 6-month period (21-215/21-355). Redemption period amended by P.A. 104-553 (eff. 7-10-26) to 3 years (1 year for vacant non-farm, 7+ unit, commercial/industrial) for certificates issued on/after that date.

changes.new: 3 years (1 year for vacant, commercial, or 7+ unit property)
changes.note: 35 ILCS 200/21-350 as amended by P.A. 104-553, eff. 7-10-26; applies to certificates issued on or after that date.

IN.sourceTitle: Monroe County (IN) Auditor - Tax Sale (cites IC 6-1.1-25-4)
IN.note: 1-year redemption (120 days for commissioner certificates); redemption at 110%/115% of minimum bid (0-6 / 6-12 months); highest bidder.

MA.note: Current §62 sets redemption interest at 8 per cent on the original sum (applied also to purchaser-held titles).

changes.note: M.G.L. c.60 §62 now reads interest at 8 per cent upon the original sum for which the land was taken or sold.

MD.note: §14-820: default redemption rate 6% (10% Calvert/Caroline/Dorchester/Garrett, 14% Carroll; many counties may set their own; owner-occupied capped at 10%); no fixed redemption deadline, foreclosure within 2 years. §14-817: sale goes to highest bid, high-bid premium may apply.

changes.note: Md. Tax-Prop. §14-817(a)(2), (b)(2): highest good faith bid; collector may require a high-bid premium.

MI.note: Foreclosed property sold at auction subject to minimum bid; conveyed to highest bidder. No post-sale redemption described.

MN.note: 3-year redemption runs from the tax judgment sale to the state, before forfeiture; forfeited land is later sold by the county with no post-sale redemption.

MO.note: Absolute right to redeem during 1 year after sale; interest not to exceed 10% annually; sold to highest bidder (140.250).

MT.note: Redemption deadline: first working day in August, 3 years after lien attaches (2 years for certain subdivided lots). Rate and bid method not re-read this run.

NC.note: Foreclosure sale by public auction to highest bidder; 10-day period after report for exceptions/increased (upset) bids.

NE.note: Redemption interest at 45-104.01 rate = 14%; tax deed application after 3 years from sale; buyer pays taxes, interest and costs, county sets bidding rules (round-robin allowed). Premium bidding not specified in statute.

NH.note: Redemption interest is 14% per annum under both tax sale (80:32) and tax lien (80:69) procedures; tax deed after 2 years (80:76). Bid method not re-read.

changes.note: RSA 80:32 and 80:69: interest at 14 percent per annum (amended 2018, 282, eff. April 1, 2019).

NJ.sourceTitle: P.L.2024, c.39 amending N.J.S.A. 54:5-86 (njleg.gov); NJ DLGS Elements of Tax Sales
NJ.note: 54:5-86 (as amended 2024): private holders may foreclose after 2 years, municipality after 6 months. DLGS: max 18%, bid down interest to 1% then bid premium; 2/4/6% redemption penalty. DLGS page dated 2011. Bid method is bid-down first, premium only after rate reaches 1%.

NV.note: After redemption period expires, deed goes to county treasurer in trust; commissioners order treasurer to sell for not less than taxes, costs, penalties and interest. No post-sale redemption.

NY.note: Default redemption expires 2 years after lien date; districts may extend (residential/farm) or shorten to 1 year for vacant/abandoned, so Varies is accurate. Rate and bid method not re-read.

OH.note: Certificate auction starts at 18% simple and bids down in 1/4% steps; holder may request foreclosure after 1 year from sale. Deed-county practice not checked.

OR.note: County holds foreclosed property 2 years from judgment for redemption, then may sell it; no redemption after county sale.

RI.note: Penalty 10% of purchase price if redeemed within 6 months, plus 1% per month after; purchaser also earns 1%/month interest on sums paid (44-9-21). 1-year period and bid method not re-read.

SC.note: Public auction; redeem within 12 months; interest 3%/6%/9%/12% of bid by quarter of redemption period (capped at bid amount).

SD.note: Lowest interest rate bid wins; no bid above 10% per year is valid. Tax deed proceeding may start after 3 years from certificate sale (within 6 years).

changes.note: SDCL 10-23-8: no rate of interest higher than ten percent per year is a valid bid.

TX.note: statutes.capitol.texas.gov refused connections during this run; no official text read.

VA.note: Sale allowed when taxes delinquent on Dec 31 after the 2nd anniversary of due date (1st for blighted/derelict); owner may redeem any time before the sale. Bid method not re-read.

VT.note: Redeem within 1 year of sale with 1% per month interest (12%/yr). Note: Vermont sells the property (deed held during redemption) rather than a lien certificate. Bid method not re-read.

WA.note: Treasurer sells to highest and best bidder, minimum bid = taxes, interest, costs; tax deed vests title (no post-sale redemption stated).
